summary: 100-foot Aermotor fire tower in Elmore County, Alabama; Register says it is now a radio relay station. Build year conflicts (1949 field, 1948 description); no staffing or access sources.

facts.status_note: In use as a radio relay station, per the Register description (2009 registration). Condition since 2009 is not reported.

events.note: Built field on the NHLR page gives 1949. The NHLR description says the Alabama Forestry Commission constructed it in 1948 (see resolved_conflicts).
Registered April 22, 2009 as US 775, AL 8; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: Register description: constructed by the Alabama Forestry Commission in 1948
evidence.quote: The 100’ Redland Fire Lookout Tower was constructed by the Alabama Forestry Commission in 1948.

evidence.quote: Now in use as a radio relay station, the Aermotor tower is in Elmore County.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR Built field gives 1949, while the NHLR description says the Alabama Forestry Commission constructed it in 1948. The event uses the structured 1949 field and the story reports both years. The sources do not explain the gap.

The Register lists the Elmore County Commission as administrator and names the Alabama Forestry Commission only as builder. The story does not say when or how administration changed, because no source does.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The NHLR page is the only tower-specific source. Two searches found no staffing, fire or access information for this tower. The Kaufmann column is statewide context and does not mention Redland; Kaufmann also nominated the tower to the Register. Build year: Built field 1949 versus description 1948, both reported. The brief elevation (547 ft, 167 m) matches the NHLR page. The OpenStreetMap node (358950411) lists a different elevation and was not used. A Wikipedia article on the Redland community has no tower mention. An anyplaceamerica.com tower page returned 403 and was not read. Not verified: current condition, public access, and when radio use began. No photos added.
